question: Locate the anchor function for the byte_array_payload field in the console.log object whose action is byte.pipe.commit, observed after entering the batch key, file name, description, category, attested profile mode, codec, shard, the normalization toggle, then clicking scan and preview, giving byte-transform consent, sealing, and clicking the final commit (upload) button on the page. The anchor function is the first target-specific byte-array transformation value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after delegated routing, scan/preview/seal gating, expanded field collection, tuple packing, byte-plan preparation and transit calculation, its own function body constructs the target observable byte-array payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or emitting to the console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, byte encoders reused outside the target path, legacy ticket reducers, gates, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice. Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends, exclusive.

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with function <function_name>( and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function with balanced braces, not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink or a payload wrapper that only emits an already constructed value.
Do not return a generic DOM reader, formatter, router, gate, tuple packer, byte utility or legacy ticket reducer when a more target-specific byte-array value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
The target behavior is byte-array transformation of the prepared upload fields, not request signing, browser fingerprinting, state encoding or request transformation.
anchor_definition_general: A function is target-specific for this task when at least one statement in its body constructs or binds the requested observable value, writes the requested field, or dispatches the requested action, and removing that statement would break the observed target output under the prescribed interaction. A function is generic when it is a reusable utility, control-flow dispatcher, scheduler, DOM/form collector, validator, serializer, normalizer or wrapper whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the shallowest target-specific function on the path from trigger to sink: upstream dispatchers are too generic, downstream reusable utilities are too low-level, and final sinks that only emit an already-built value are wrappers rather than anchors.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example from a different scenario: a checkout page emits body.order_sig_v2 after Submit Order. The chain collects an order draft, encodes checkout state, collects an async profile receipt, composes a request envelope, runs a generic interceptor pipeline, then selects a sealing interceptor. The sealing interceptor is the anchor because its immediate caller is a generic dispatcher and its own body is the highest point that explains why order_sig_v2 is produced. Helpers below it that canonicalize fields or fold payload bytes are nested target-specific helpers; the digest routine is a reusable core utility; the dispatcher and request sender are wrappers or path functions; same-click analytics_sig or retry_fingerprint values are off-chain decoys. Apply the same reasoning to the actual page and bundle below.
notes: The page stages a deterministic local upload manifest and writes the observable object to the browser console.
The target value is a deterministic byte-array transformation of the prepared upload fields, not an environment digest.

The final commit path is gated by a valid batch key, attested profile mode, a non-plain codec, a non-default shard, the normalize toggle, the scan action, the preview action, explicit consent, and the seal action.
The final field name may be reconstructed dynamically at runtime.
Decoy console outputs may appear before the requested log object.
Several byte-like reducer outputs are retained as near misses but do not feed the requested field.
